teams.heading: Fiji take level six-all record against Italy into Saturday's Udine test
teams.body: The ledger with the Azzurri could hardly be tighter: across 12 meetings, Fiji and Italy have six wins apiece, according to OnRugby. The sides have not met since November 2017, when Italy won 19-10 in Catania. Both arrive in Udine without a Nations Championship win and bottom of their respective pools, and the Italian outlet reckons they could well meet again in London on the tournament's final weekend. Fiji come off a 15-43 defeat to Ireland in Dublin, where they failed to score in the second half.

lead.why: The only item centred on Fiji's own test, and its six-all head-to-head angle has not run in an earlier edition.

teams.heading: Five-try Will Joseph tipped to keep England wing against All Blacks
teams.body: Gloucester wing Will Joseph was understood, in a BBC report on 16 November, to be in pole position for Saturday's Nations Championship test against New Zealand, with Immanuel Feyi-Waboso ruled out of the autumn by an ankle injury. Joseph's five tries in the 78-15 win over Japan, including a hat-trick inside 19 minutes, made him only the fifth England men's player to score five in one match. Cadan Murley is the squad's other specialist wing. "He floats, doesn't he?" said England team-mate Ben Earl.

teams.heading: Fabien Galthié recalls Matthieu Jalibert at fly-half and overhauls France's back row
teams.body: France head coach Fabien Galthié has made four changes for Saturday's Round 6 test against Argentina at the Stade de France. Bordeaux-Bègles' Matthieu Jalibert starts at No. 10 in his first outing of any kind since September after injury, sending Maxime Lucu to the bench. In the back row, Anthony Jelonch returns at No. 8 between flankers Charles Ollivon and Esteban Capilla, with Grégory Alldritt and Cameron Woki dropping to the replacements. Louis Bielle-Biarrey, managed during the week, keeps his place on the wing.

lead.why: The France team to face Argentina is announced, with a fly-half recall and an entirely new back row.

teams.heading: Ireland captain Dan Sheehan tipped to start at No. 8 against Springboks
teams.body: According to The 42, Ireland head coach Andy Farrell is expected to move his captain from hooker to the back of the scrum for Saturday's test against South Africa, with Caelan Doris, Jack Conan and Sean Jansen all unavailable. Sheehan, back from the concussion that kept him out of the 43-15 win over Fiji, has never started a test at No. 8 but impressed there for Leinster against Munster in the URC last month. The switch would free Rónan Kelleher to start at hooker between Andrew Porter and Tadhg Furlong.

lead.why: A new Ireland selection story: the captain is tipped to switch from hooker to No. 8 against the Springboks.

teams.heading: Gonzalo Quesada names Italy side for Fiji and confirms Domingo's opportunity
teams.body: Italy head coach Gonzalo Quesada has announced his side for the Round 6 Nations Championship test against Fiji at Udine's Bluenergy Stadium. He used his press conference to confirm that Domingo will get his chance. Quesada said the plan from the outset had been to play him against Fiji, then weigh whether to start him. He also called Fiji a side with quality and said he expects a tight game. Italy go into the weekend 11th of 12, still winless after a 14-19 defeat to Argentina.

lead.why: The federation's Udine report also carries the team announcement and Quesada's selection comments, which is fresh Italy news and not the already-reported hospital visit.

teams.heading: Scotland turn to Tom Jordan to fill Finn Russell gap before Japan
teams.body: Tom Jordan gets the call to cover for fly-half Finn Russell before Saturday's Nations Championship finale against Japan, and there is more bad news up front: a Scotland forward is undergoing an operation. The squad was already stretched: captain Sione Tuipulotu, scrum-half Ben White, number eight Jack Dempsey and lock Scott Cummings were ruled out of the Japan game earlier in the week, with Edinburgh forwards Grant Gilchrist and Magnus Bradbury and Leicester lock Cam Henderson called up. Glasgow's Rory Darge now captains the squad.

lead.why: Fresh Scotland selection and injury news before the Japan game; the stronger new item over a pundit's view or an old fine.

teams.heading: Steve Tandy drops All Blacks player of the match Botham against Australia
teams.body: Wales head coach Steve Tandy has left Cardiff flanker James Botham out of the matchday 23 for Saturday's test against Australia, with Alex Mann starting at blindside. Botham was player of the match in last weekend's 35-28 win over New Zealand, Wales's first against the All Blacks since 1953. His partner is expecting their first child this week, but Tandy insisted that was not part of the selection decision. He said Botham spent Tuesday's training session "leading the charge, running opposition plays for Australia, and bringing unbelievable intensity."

lead.why: The confirmed team leaves out last week's player of the match, and Tandy explained the call; Thursday's edition covered only the expected recalls.

teams.heading: Julián Montoya returns as captain in seven Pumas changes for France
teams.body: Head coach Felipe Contepomi has reshaped his side after last week's 19-14 win over Italy. Montoya, the captain, missed that game and now takes the hooker's shirt from the injured Bautista Bernasconi for Saturday's Nations Championship meeting with France. Tomás Lavanini replaces Pedro Rubiolo at lock. Juan Martín González is restored to the back row and Pablo Matera drops to the bench. Facundo Isa starts at No. 8, which moves Juan Martín Scelzo to openside. Gerónimo Prisciantelli takes over at full-back, and Rodrigo Isgró moves to the bench.

lead.why: Argentina's team announcement for France is today's fresh Argentina event, with the captain back and seven changes.

teams.heading: Les Kiss drops Fraser McReight to bench in five-change Wallabies pack
teams.body: Fraser McReight, the reigning John Eales Medal winner, drops to the bench with Carlo Tizzano starting at openside as Wallabies coach Les Kiss reshapes the pack for Saturday's Nations Championship Test against Wales. The whole front row is new, with Isaac Kailea, Brandon Paenga-Amosa and Taniela Tupou promoted from the bench, while Tom Hooper makes his first Test start at lock in almost a year, ahead of Jeremy Williams. The backline is untouched from the 12-15 defeat to Scotland, and prop Allan Alaalatoa is in line for a 99th cap as a replacement.

lead.why: Benching the reigning John Eales Medal winner is the headline of a five-change Wallabies pack overhaul.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones names new front row and Komura at fly-half against Scotland
teams.body: Japan head coach Eddie Jones has rung the changes for Saturday's pool finale against Scotland at Murrayfield. With props Keijiro Tamafusa and Opeti Helu, Shuhei Takeuchi and Riku Tokito out through injury or condition, and centre Dylan Riley absent for personal reasons, a new front row starts. Jack Cornelsen comes in at lock for Harry Hockings, sent off against England; Faulua Makisi starts at No. 8 and Shinya Komura at fly-half. Taufa Latu, Nicholas McCullan and Halatoa Vailea are the squad call-ups.

teams.heading: Rennie makes eight changes for England with Beauden Barrett set for 150th cap
teams.body: All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has recalled Codie Taylor, Damian McKenzie, Cam Roigard, Jordie Barrett and Will Jordan among his changes for Saturday's Test against England at Twickenham. Richie Mo’unga, Cortez Ratima and Asafo Aumua drop to the bench after the 35-28 defeat to Wales. Taylor takes the captaincy back from Beauden Barrett, who starts at full-back and will become only the fourth player to reach 150 Test caps. A bonus-point win would book New Zealand's place in the Nations Championship final.

lead.why: It is the All Blacks' team announcement for England, reported by two outlets: a sweeping response to the Wales defeat and Beauden Barrett's 150th cap.

teams.heading: Sir Steve Hansen defends banned Rassie Erasmus, calls officials a 'protected beast'
teams.body: Former All Blacks head coach Sir Steve Hansen told the For The Love of Rugby podcast that match officials are a "protected beast". He blamed World Rugby rules that bar test coaches from one-on-one pre-match talks with referees for the frustration behind Springbok head coach Rassie Erasmus' outburst. Erasmus drew a six-match ban for questioning the officiating after the 21-19 defeat to France in Paris. Hansen judged the attack calculated and accepted there were consequences. The suspension keeps Erasmus out of the Aviva Stadium for Saturday's Ireland test.

lead.why: The highest-ranked new take on the Erasmus ban that has not already led, and the one a fan would forward.
